title: Bhagat Singh Series in Development at Collective Studios' Historyverse
excerpt: Collective Artists Network's Historyverse banner is developing a series on Indian freedom fighter Bhagat Singh, expanding its slate of Indian history-inspired content for global audiences.
body:
• Collective Studios' Historyverse is developing a series based on the life of Indian revolutionary Bhagat Singh
  • The project is part of Historyverse's expanding slate of Indian history-inspired content, which includes titles based on figures like Hanuman, Krishna, Shiva, and Shivaji
  • Historyverse has already partnered with Zee 5 for six AI-driven originals and positions itself as India's largest history-inspired content initiative
  • The Bhagat Singh series marks Historyverse's first foray into India's freedom struggle narrative

Collective Studios' Historyverse, the Indian history-inspired content initiative under Collective Artists Network, is developing a series on revolutionary freedom fighter Bhagat Singh. The project marks a significant expansion for Historyverse, which has until now focused primarily on mythological and ancient historical figures.

From Mythology to Freedom Struggle

Historyverse launched earlier this year with a slate of eight titles drawn from India's mythological and historical traditions, including stories inspired by Hanuman, Krishna, Shiva, Shivaji, Durga, Kali, and Swami Samarth. The Mahabharat series served as the starting point for the banner's larger vision of bringing historically rooted Indian narratives to modern screens.

https://x.com/Variety/status/2087743466520432905

The Bhagat Singh series represents the first time Historyverse is venturing into India's modern freedom struggle. Bhagat Singh, executed by the British colonial government in 1931 at the age of 23, remains one of India's most revered revolutionary figures — an atheist intellectual, a socialist thinker, and a symbol of youthful defiance against colonial oppression.

"I've always believed that our folklore is among the richest in the world, and that these stories, woven into the core of our cultural fabric, deserve a global stage."

— Vijay Subramaniam, Founder and Group CEO, Collective Artists Network

A Growing Content Ecosystem

Historyverse has been building momentum rapidly. The banner recently partnered with Zee 5 to unveil six AI-driven originals inspired by Indian mythology and history, set to premiere across seven languages including Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Malayalam, Kannada, and Bangla. A separate project, Vikram Betal, is being developed as an AI-powered show reimagining India's storytelling traditions, with an educational partnership with Birla Open Minds.

Vijay Subramaniam, the founder and Group CEO of Collective Artists Network, has positioned Historyverse as more than a production slate — envisioning an ecosystem that extends into gaming, consumer brands, and immersive experiences built around Indian historical narratives.

Why Bhagat Singh Resonates Globally

Multiple filmmakers and production houses have explored Bhagat Singh's story over the years, including Rajkumar Santoshi's acclaimed 2002 film "The Legend of Bhagat Singh" starring Ajay Devgn. Director Gurvinder Singh, known for his Cannes and Venice-premiering Punjabi films, has separately been developing a web series focused on Bhagat Singh's trial and its political dimensions.

What sets the Historyverse approach apart is its focus on scale and contemporary storytelling formats. The project aims to present Bhagat Singh's story not as a linear biographical narrative but with the layered, immersive treatment that has become the Historyverse signature — deeply researched scripts paired with modern visual and narrative techniques designed for streaming audiences in India and internationally.

For the Indian diaspora, Bhagat Singh holds particular resonance. His writings on colonialism, socialism, and self-determination have been rediscovered by younger generations, and a well-produced series could introduce his ideas to global audiences unfamiliar with India's independence movement beyond Gandhi and Nehru.

What's Next

Details on the series' cast, director, and streaming platform have not been announced. Given Historyverse's existing partnership with Zee 5 and its multi-language distribution strategy, the Bhagat Singh project is likely to follow a similar path. Production timelines have not been disclosed, but the project's inclusion in the Historyverse slate signals it has moved beyond concept stage into active development.
